questions.questionText:
Which characteristic relates to perfect competition and which to monopoly?
perfect competition monopoly

options.text: barriers to entry freedom of entry

questions.questionText:
Cocoa and sugar are used in a factory to produce chocolate.
What is a fixed cost in the production of chocolate?

In August 2008, Infosys, an Indian information technology company, bought Axon, a UK
information technology company.
Which type of integration is this?

The multinational Indian Tata Group, which has companies in chemicals, consumer goods,
engineering and communications, has been buying foreign companies.
What does this action most likely suggest about the company?

options.text: It intends to achieve a domestic monopoly position.
It intends to increase its level of specialisation.
It intends to reduce fixed costs.
It intends to spread risks by diversification.

questions.questionText: What is the most likely result of an increase in interest rates?
What is most likely to be the responsibility of a central government?

options.text: the provision of immigration officials at an airport
the provision of security cameras in a shopping centre
the provision of security staff at a bank
the provision of ticket inspectors on a train

questions.questionText:
In the first six months of 2011 a construction company, Morgan Sindall, saw its profits fall. Part of
the reason was the increased competition from foreign competitors.
Which government policy is most likely to help such a company?

options.text: increasing tax-free allowances on new building projects
putting a quota on imported raw materials used by the company

questions.questionText:
The graph shows the impact of a tax on the supply of petrol (gas).
D S
price 1
quantity
What can be concluded from this graph?

options.text: the government will receive no tax revenue
the impact of the tax will be shared between the consumer and the producer
the impact of the tax will fall entirely upon the consumer
the impact of the tax will fall entirely on the producer

questions.questionText:
A tractor factory runs out of important components and has to stop production.
How does this illustrate the economic problem?

options.text: The factory lacks a competitive advantage.
The factory lacks economies of scale.
There is evidence of scarce resources.

questions.questionText: Which group linked to a firm always bears the risk of the decision to produce?

In a pure market economy, which secondary factor determines the distribution of goods and
services?

Maize and fuel are used in the production of Mexican tortillas. In 2010 Mexico produced a record
maize crop but in 2011 rises in the price of fuel increased costs for tortilla makers.
What is likely to have happened to the price of tortillas in 2010 and 2011?
price in 2010 price in 2011

When the price of shirts rises from $8 to $10, the demand for shirts falls from 1000 to 500.
What is the price elasticity of demand for shirts?
What is a likely reason why many countries’ governments subsidise scientific research?

options.text: Private sector firms may overestimate the external benefits and ignore the private benefits of scientific research.
Private sector firms may overestimate the external costs and ignore the private costs of scientific research.
Private sector firms may underestimate the private benefits and ignore the external benefits of scientific research.
Private sector firms may underestimate the private costs and ignore the external costs of scientific research.

questions.questionText:
When the price of a good doubles the demand falls by less than half, and the revenue received
by the seller increases.
What does this suggest about the good?

options.text: it is perfectly elastic in demand

questions.questionText: The use of a mobile (cell) phone to make payments is an example of which function of money?

What is most likely to cause a person to save a larger proportion of their weekly income rather
than spend a larger proportion of their weekly income?

options.text: a decrease in the tax on goods and services
an increase in the range of products available

questions.questionText: Which of the following is most likely to limit wage increases in an industry?

options.text: an increased demand for the industry’s product
a rise in the industry’s profits
a rise in wages for workers in similar jobs
the replacement of workers with robots

questions.questionText: What is a function of a trade union?

options.text: to promote workers to more responsible jobs
to recruit workers for the firm
to supervise the workers in the firm

questions.questionText:
Differences in earnings between higher paid and lower paid jobs have widened in developed
countries.
What is the most likely reason for this?

options.text: Immigration of unskilled workers has reduced.
The demand for highly skilled workers has increased.
Women are paid the same rates as men.

questions.questionText: What is thought to be a benefit of global free trade?

options.text: It increases the opportunity for domestic producers to specialise.
It increases the protection for domestic producers.
It reduces a country’s reliance on other countries.
It reduces the transport costs involved in trading.

questions.questionText:
The table gives the retail price of a paperback book as printed on its back cover.
United Kingdom £6.99
Canada $11.99 (Canadian dollars)
Australia $14.99 (Australian dollars)
New Zealand $20.95 (New Zealand dollars)
What is needed to make a clear comparison of the price in the four countries?

The table shows the percentage share of GDP held by the richest 20% and poorest 20% of the
population in each country.
Which country had the greatest extremes of income and poverty?
country richest 20% poorest 20%

On 17 October 2006, the US population reached 300 million and was predicted to increase to
400million by 2043.
Which change would mean that the US population moves in the opposite direction to that
predicted?

options.text: a change from net immigration to net emigration
the birth rate falling more slowly than the death rate
the death rate falling below the net immigration rate
the infant mortality rate decreasing more rapidly than the increase in life expectancy

questions.questionText:
What is most likely to be an indicator that a country is a developed economy rather than a
developing economy?

options.text: a low level of adult literacy

questions.questionText:
In developed economies there are changing patterns of employment.
What explains why fewer work in agriculture but food production has increased?

options.text: mechanisation and the use of scientific methods
movement to factory jobs in manufacturing
shift to office work using computers

questions.questionText:
The table gives information about some economic indicators in a number of countries.
inflation interest rates unemployment
% % %
country W 1.4 3.4 10.2
country X 3.7 8.7 12.3
country Y 3.6 7.3 14.2
country Z 2.1 6.0 7.7
What may be concluded from this information?

options.text: Countries with higher inflation have higher interest rates.
Countries with higher interest rates have lower inflation.
The country with the lowest inflation had the highest unemployment.

The country with the lowest unemployment had the highest inflation.
